description: ARNAD is the aeronautical navigation database maintained by the TsAI aeronautical information centre that publishes the Russian Federation's AIP. It is built for onboard navigation systems, satellite navigation and landing systems, flight planning and air traffic control systems and navigation simulators, and is kept to the ARINC 424 standard. It covers ten world zones (Africa, Canada, Eastern Europe, Europe, Latin America, Asia, Pacific, South America, South Pacific and the USA); it includes aerodromes with runways of 1,500 metres or more with their departure, arrival and approach procedures, radio navigation aids, airways, holding patterns, control areas and restricted zones and minimum safe altitudes, with all aerodromes in the CIS countries published in TsAI documents; custom records add magnetic variation grids and route and aerodrome obstacles. Data are updated continuously and delivered per AIRAC cycle on CD-ROM, by e-mail or over the internet, in formats set by the customer's navigation system. Access is paid under a signed licence agreement, priced by the volume of records selected. Caveats: coverage outside the CIS is limited to larger aerodromes, and the pages are in Russian. The database supports airspace and airport network models and hazard exposure studies of navigation infrastructure, and is related to the FAA aeronautical data (NASR) for the United States.
